# BOOK 1: Cole of Spyglass Mountain (Arthur Preston Hankins, 1923)

## Characters
- **Joshua "Josh" Cole** (Cole; Tony; 56-35 / Fifty-six thirty-five in House of Refuge; later "Cole of Spyglass Mountain"): gray-blue eyes, black hair, ascetic face. Loves astronomy/science. Tolerant, stubborn, fights when cornered.
- **Lester Cole**: younger brother (11 at start), black-haired, cowardly-ish, later works in shoe store; refuses to help Joshua; Lester's 21st birthday June 15.
- **John Cole**: father, traveling hardware salesman, drinker, gambler (ponies), cruel; ducks Joshua's head in bathtub; has Joshua committed to House of Refuge.
- **Blanche Florence Cole**: mother, from Maryland Florence family; dies (Joshua arrives too late). Joshua's "poor boy" line.
- **Silvanus Madmallet** ("Ole Hothatchet/Sorehammer/Madhouse"): austere teacher; Joshua threatens him with iron poker; expels him.
- **Slinky Dawson**: teacher's pet, carries note; Joshua intercepts it.
- **Zida Hunt**: Coles' Black cook/maid, friend to Joshua.
- **Spud Mulligan, "Did" Eustace**: gang friends.
- **Madge (Shanty Madge) Mundy**: red-gold frizzly hair, Oriental-topaz/brown-red eyes, Pocahontas coloring; gypo queen; daughter of Bloodmop.
- **George "Bloodmop" Mundy**: fiery red hair, sky-blue eyes, gypo contractor; dies ~3 months before Part 2 events (heart? unspecified).
- **Elizabeth Mundy**: Madge's mother, refined, dark-haired, "'Lizabeth."
- **Detective Dickinson**: plainclothes man who finds Joshua at gypo camp; kind.
- **Judge** (police judge): blond, fat, "Tk-tk-tk."
- **Superintendent** of House of Refuge: grandson-relation; Peter D. Florence founded it.
- **Beaver Clegg**: ugly-but-kind head of Juvenile Department, variable-star observer, 3-inch refractor; teaches Joshua astronomy on roof at night; dies of heart failure; leaves Joshua telescope, books, photos.
- **Number 23-44 / Felix "Slim" Wolfgang**: Norwegian, freckled, sandy hair, gambler; in House of Refuge with Joshua; hires The Whimperer to trail Joshua; shoots Joshua (thirty-thirty rifle) near camp; later plots with Lee Sweet; later Winnie the Weeper is his girl.
- **The Whimperer** (John Yegg, "De Whimperer"; real name unstated): scarred cheek (acid), twisted mouth, fake crippled arm, whimperpoem card; "whimpermeter"; steals Joshua's telescope, sells for $100; Joshua's jocker; later drunk on wagon; writes letters.
- **California Bill Fox** ("Ole California Bill"): freighter, squat, broad hat, slate-gray eyes, iron-gray hair, black brows, six-mule outfit; former deputy sheriff; "Cole of Spyglass Mountain" named by him; gives Joshua $40 loan; confronts Slim with pistol; rides to Sweet.
- **Lee Sweet**: big bearded Box-R Ranch cattleman, drunk, fires rifle at Joshua's cabin/observatory; burns cabin; wrecks Argo's graze.
- **Mr. John Golden**: mining engineer at G-string.
- **Jack Montgomery**: son of Montgomery (Montgomery & Applegate); Madge's suitor; marries Madge eventually.
- **Mary Montgomery**: Jack's sister.
- **Philip Demarest** (Demarest, Spruce and Tillou contractors); **Spruce**, **Tillou**; **Jawbone Mahoney**: boss powderman whose overshot shot caused slide; **Bluenose**: Joshua's crewman; **Emanuel Peters**/Branscomb: engineers.
- **Steve**: walking boss.
- **Winnie the Weeper**: Slim's girl.
- **Dr. J. Miles Stanhope**: drunk hospital doctor at Ragtown.
- **Argo**: Joshua's dapple gray horse (bought for $500, formerly "Prince").
- **Hopkins**? (Not Book 1.)

## Plot Events (Book 1, chronological)
1. Spring, city lot: Joshua and Lester watch slug (*Limax campestris*) lower itself from chip on string of mucus. Teacher Madmallet punishes Lester; Joshua threatens him with poker; expelled; Lester suspended a week.
2. Joshua fetches father's razor; slug walks razor edge. Joshua intercepts Slinky Dawson's note (Mrs. John H. Cole, 355 Grant Avenue).
3. Crescent Skating Rink: Joshua meets Madge Mundy (gypo camp by railroad tracks). Lester leaves. Joshua sleeps in boxcar; joins Mundy camp; Bloodmop offers grading work; Madge and Joshua talk stars (Orion, Big Dipper, Pointer, Pole Star).
4. Dickinson arrests Joshua at camp; John Cole has him committed to House of Refuge (age until 21; "Number 5635"; later "56-35" / "Fifty-six thirty-five" — text uses both).
5. House of Refuge: Clegg tutors him on roof: moon craters Clavius, Tycho, Blancanus. Joshua wins two T-and-H medals; fights and beats 23-44 (Wolfgang) to break parole. Stays until 21.
6. Clegg dies. Joshua pardoned at 20 (some say 21 at end); goes West, Lester refuses help.
7. Joshua leaves on freight; meets The Whimperer; tramps for a year; Whimperer steals telescope in Kansas/Colorado area; Joshua starves in Southern Colorado; slug moment → "unique tramp" philosophy; prays.
8. Spur, Gold Belt Cut-off railroad (San Antonio Range). Joshua hired by Demarest, Spruce & Tillou; meets California Bill Fox.
9. Joshua finds Madge at Camp One, meets Elizabeth; plans homestead on Spyglass Mountain near Stirrup Lake; buys clothes ($17.35). Bloodmop dead; Madge "Shanty Madge" runs outfit; tunnel at Hill of Springs slides.
10. Bill helps Joshua file homestead at Los Angeles land office.
11. Joshua shot (left shoulder, low, near heart) at dusk near Camp; Dr. Stanhope treats at Ragtown hospital.
12. Joshua's coyote-hole plan (triangle diagram A–I, "work behind the pressure") stops slide; wins $5,000; refuses Demarest's job offer.
13. Joshua buys 8-inch telescope ($2,000 from journal ad), buys dapple gray Argo ($500). Mundys move to homestead. Lee Sweet confronts Joshua at Ragtown water trough; Bill intervenes.
14. Slim Wolfgang shown at Ragtown; The Whimperer confesses on wagon: Slim paid him, Whimperer sold telescope for $100, Slim shot Joshua.
15. Madge reveals love for Jack Montgomery (in Los Angeles); Joshua proposes at campfire; she refuses ("you're a dreamer").
16. Cabin, observatory built; Joshua publishes articles (Universe, American Astronomer, Journal of Astronomy "Cole of Spyglass Mountain," "Is Mars a Lifeless Planet?"). Scientific controversy.
17. Lee Sweet fires on observatory and cabin; Joshua's Argo stampeded by cattle.
18. Madge's letter (June 14): will marry Jack Montgomery. Joshua remembers Lester's birthday June 15.
19. Joshua observes Mars night of June 18 (not June 15 as chapter title says); sees faint geometric figure; Lee Sweet shoots at dome; Joshua falls.
20. Bill finds Slim/Winnie on June 15 night, captures Slim at gunpoint; Slim confesses: conspiracy with John Cole; Peter Henry Florence legacy $150,000 to Joshua at 21 (Lester if Joshua dies); Slim paid $15,000 to keep Joshua away.
21. Bill rides to Lee Sweet; Joshua hospitalized at Ragtown; telegram to Dr. Buck, Milton University; Dr. Emanuel Schlott (German) photographs same figure; Joshua acclaimed.
22. Madge returns; reconciles with Joshua ("I've come back to Spyglass Mountain").

## Key Details / Quotes
- "You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain."
- Slim: "Joshua" aside; "Fifty-six thirty-five."
- Bloodmop: "Well, I'm a son-of-a-gun!"
- Joshua's brother Lester's birthday: June 15; Lester's 21st.
- Mars opposition: June 18 (42 million miles).
- Telescope: Brashear, 8-inch; observatory conical revolving metal dome; cost $300 home-made design; article $25.
- Spyglass Mountain ~7,750 ft; Stirrup Lake ~6,750 ft.

# BOOK 2: The Crow's Inn Tragedy (Annie Haynes, 1927)

## Characters
- **Luke Francis Bechcombe**: solicitor, Bechcombe & Turner, 21 Crow's Inn; murdered (strangled, chloroform, gloved) ~noon on a day in early Feb (Feb 3rd per Todmarsh's arrest warrant). Small, grey, horn-rimmed glasses, neat grey beard.
- **Madeline Bechcombe** (Mrs. Luke), Carlsford Square; regal, dark, flashing eyes; "Sadie" is Mrs. Phillimore's nickname.
- **Rev. James Collyer**: rector of Wexbridge; brother-in-law of Luke; keeps Collyer emerald cross (paste substituted).
- **Anthony "Tony" Collyer**: son of rector; D.S.O. WWI veteran; gassed, wounded; in love with Cecily Hoyle; suspected of murder; later gets job as secretary to invalid young Bramley (Sir John Bramley's son; Bramley Hall near Burford).
- **Aubrey Todmarsh**: nephew of Luke, son of old Aubrey Todmarsh; conscientious objector; founder of Confraternity of St. Philip (South London Settlement); real identity **the Yellow Dog**, head of Yellow Gang; arrested at end; cyanide attempt foiled.
- **Cecily Frances Hoyle**: Luke's secretary; daughter of Christopher/John Frederick Hoyle; photographed by Thompson; stays at Hobart Residence, Windover Square; later revealed to be daughter of Dr. James Hoyle by mother's first marriage.
- **Amos Thompson** / **Samuel Horsingforth** / **John Frederick Hoyle** / "Mr. Hoyle of Rose Cottage, Burford": managing clerk; fraudster; second identity; arrested at Southampton on boat (Atlantic) bound for Lisbon; 10 Brooklyn Terrace, North Kensington; room near Brooklyn Terrace; chloroform used? (no—Todmarsh did).
- **Inspector William Furnival** ("The Ferret," Scotland Yard, C.I.D.).
- **John Steadman, K.C.** (barrister; Mrs. Bechcombe's cousin; Luke's cousin); keen cross-examiner.
- **Dr. Hackett**: doctor summoned to Crow's Inn.
- **Mrs. Cyril B. Carnthwacke** (formerly Bella Laymond, Variety stage): American millionaire's wife (Cyril B. Carnthwacke); gambler; pawned diamonds (Russian crown-jewel necklace); went to Luke's office at ~12:30 but receipt; attacked in own car (strangled, Bond Street area; Victoria Gate, Hyde Park) — survives, pretends dying.
- **Mrs. Phillimore** (Sadie; American widow; alias Fédora, fortune-teller; real criminal from Boston; arrested).
- **Hopkins**: Todmarsh's man; arrested at Whistone Hall burglary; wife rescued Steadman's car episode; later reveals Todmarsh's plans.
- **John Walls**, **Spencer** (William Spencer), **Percy Johnson**, **Brunton** (19, office boy → clerk).
- **Mrs. Wye**: housekeeper at Rose Cottage, Burford.
- Landlord of Royal Arms, Burford.
- **Masterman**: police agent on train.
- **Mrs. Walls**, **Jones** (inspector's subordinate), **Murphy**, **Jackson**, **Gordon** (carpenter).

## Plot Events (Book 2)
1. Opening: Rev. James Collyer visits Luke about Tony's debts; sells emerald cross via Luke. Luke discovers emeralds are paste; cross left in Luke's safe.
2. Todmarsh's Settlement, St. Philip's; Aubrey on conscientious objectors; Michael Farmore arrest.
3. Morning of murder: Thompson's absence; Tony pushes into Luke's room; Cecily leaves at 11:45; Luke found dead ~12:00; body behind screen; Cecily hears movement 1:30 on return.
4. Inspector Furnival: glove (white suède, French) found; Dr. Hackett estimates death ~12 noon.
5. Mrs. Carnthwacke comes forward; says she saw Bechcombe ~12:30–1 p.m., left diamonds, receipt signed "Luke Francis Bechcombe"; her description of man differs (taller, bald, different hands—long thumb, short forefinger).
6. Burford visit: Inspector and Steadman find Rose Cottage (Mr. Hoyle, artist); signature "Christopher Hoyle" painted over.
7. Yellow Gang / Yellow Dog; "chink-a-pin" password; 21 Burlase Street, Limehouse.
8. Steadman and inspector captured by Yellow Gang; stripped; escape via river window; note from informant.
9. Carnthwacke's wife attacked in car; survives.
10. Todmarsh arrested at Community House when greeted Hopkins's car; cyanide attempt foiled (inspector substituted tabloids).
11. Thompson arrested aboard Atlantic; revealed as Samuel Horsingforth / John Frederick Hoyle.
12. Ending: Tony and Cecily reconcile; "And Anthony... confessed that he thought it was."

## Key Facts / Numbers
- Office: 21 Crow's Inn (corner house, Crow's Inn Square).
- Brooklyn Terrace No. 10, North Kensington.
- Carlsford Square: Bechcombe house.
- Hobart Residence, Windover Square.
- Field of Rest (St. Philip's churchyard).
- Rose Cottage, Burford (New Forest).
- Telegram: "Do not mention home address. Father." (Edgware Road PO, March 4th).
- Proof: Mrs. Carnthwacke's diamond receipt signed "Luke Francis Bechcombe."
- Mrs. Carnthwacke's assailant was Todmarsh (thumb long, forefinger short).
